Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the right-opening parabola shown above. Express the answer in terms of the variable $y.$

$\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola has its vertex at $O,$ and passes through the point $(8,-8).$

The standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(0,0)$ is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Substituting $x=8$ and $y=-8$ into the equation above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-8)^{2} & =4p(8) \\ 64 & =32p \\ p & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of our parabola is 

$$
{y}^{2}=8x.
$$

Finally, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(8x) \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =8 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{4}{y}\end{aligned}
$$
